R350.note: Adds correct bounds check before array write; silently dropping out-of-range indices is fine since none are ever valid for a 16-slot table.

R351.note: execFile with argument array closes the shell injection; the disclosed leading-'-' rejection cannot exclude any legal domain name.

R352.note: Moves the state-changing delete off GET onto DELETE wrapped in CrossOriginProtection, the correct fix for this vulnerability class; the loss of one-click email-link deletion is the vulnerability itself and is stated plainly.

R353.note: Case is that @EnableMethodSecurity is missing so @PreAuthorize never runs anywhere; fix hand-rolls a manual check only inside deleteUserAccount instead of fixing SecurityConfig, leaving the identical, still-unenforced @PreAuthorize on suspendUserAccount unprotected.

R354.note: Replaces manual inline-protocol string construction with EnyimMemcachedCore's typed Store() API, removing the injection surface; explanation misnames the memcached binary protocol as 'RESP-like' but the fix itself is sound.

R355.note: Magic-byte check plus random-UUID storage correctly closes the upload weakness, but the added filename-extension allowlist is a new gate not required by the contract and could reject a genuine PNG/JPEG whose client-supplied filename lacks a recognized extension; disclosed as 'Layer 1'.

R356.note: Adds permission_classes = [IsAdminUser], closing the AllowAny default; queryset was never user-scoped so an admin-only management API is the reasonable read of intended access.

R357.note: Contract requires nested archive entries to still extract, but the added single-path-component check (equesting entryName to equal its own getFileName()) rejects every entry containing a '/', i.e. all nested entries, not just traversal attempts; disclosed but breaks required legitimate behavior wholesale.

R358.note: toRealPath() plus startsWith containment check on both target and base correctly rejects absolute/escaping paths while still serving any file genuinely inside BASE_DIR, matching the contract.

R359.note: can:refund,order middleware plus an ownership-based Policy runs before the controller and matches the contract; authorized owners still get the same response shape.

R360.note: Explicit CRLF rejection closes the SMTP command injection; the added email-format regex is scoped to a field literally named customerEmail, a reasonable domain-defined format rather than an arbitrary security-only allowlist.

R361.note: UUID-derived filename, storage outside the static webroot, and a validated serving route close the traversal/dangerous-type vector while still returning a fetchable url and the same 400 error shape for unsupported types.

R362.note: Table name is now taken only from a server-owned allowlist map rather than raw request text, accountId/status remain bound params, and the default ledger_entries path still works, matching the contract.

R363.note: subprocess.run with an argument list and shell=False removes shell interpretation and preserves the original log-write-then-read response shape; no extra host-format restriction added.

R364.note: Replaces raw-socket SELECT string building with Jakarta Mail's Store/Folder API, which frames the folder name as data instead of protocol syntax; open(READ_WRITE) matches the original SELECT's implicit read-write semantics.

R365.note: escapeshellarg() around the host argument is the minimal, correct fix for shell_exec concatenation and changes nothing else observable.
